method: Static inspection, Rizin/Capstone disassembly, Unicorn emulation with mocked Windows APIs, LZNT1 recovery, import-name XOR decoding, source-map recovery and upstream comparison. No specimen ran as a native process; no emulated network action was implemented.

samples.identification: Adobe Creative Cloud Set-Up 6.11.0.479 with two Expiro-style parasitic native loaders
samples.marker_line: Adobe setup: grafted native loaders; add behavior coverage
evidence: Host version resources, manifest and Jenkins PDB identify Adobe Creative Cloud Set-Up, not the many unrelated family names in the collector filename. The host is unsigned; its checksum is valid. Checksum mismatch is not required for these detections.

Entry 0x59e390 calls 0x401011, whose patched 0x401037 PUSHAD stub uses the return address to locate VirtualAlloc and an encrypted resource buffer. Executable instructions are scattered between ordinary host functions and connected by jumps.

At 0x401111 a byte is loaded and adjusted by 0xa1; at 0x401291/0x401301/0x401321 a word is copied and adjusted by -0x206a. Further mixed-width operations reconstruct bytes in an allocation. Keys and branch offsets are wildcarded in the detection.

At 0x404036/0x404143 the loader sets up PAGE_EXECUTE_READ and the reconstructed buffer. VirtualProtect is reached at 0x404179; 0x404184 preserves the buffer argument, adds the entry offset, and 0x4041a2 calls it. Emulation reached 0x20061938 after reconstructing into the first allocation.

The subsequent CRT path 0x59e212 has a patched call at 0x59e219 to 0x88f000 in the second .rsrc. That section is RWX and near-random. The stub derives a base with call/pop EAX, transforms 0x400-byte blocks through unrolled add/subtract/XOR/NOT operations, and calls 0x84c5b8 at 0x88f8d1.

Both loader paths resolve APIs by walking loaded-module exports and hashing uppercased names with ROL19/add. Recomputed hashes identify RtlDecompressBuffer, VirtualAlloc, VirtualProtect, GetProcAddress, LoadLibraryA and other APIs. A first-stage CreateFileW call attempts C:\Mirc\mirc.ini; its wider purpose was not established.

RtlDecompressBuffer(format 0x102) produces 0x62200- and 0x80c00-byte native DLL images. Both start with PNG magic, carry a shifted NT-header pointer at offset eight, and erase the PE signature. Reconstruction of normal PE headers was solely an analysis aid; those reconstructed files are not claimed to be original binaries.

The custom mapper decrypts module and import names with a per-build 256-byte digit-valued XOR table, maps sections, resolves imports and changes protections. The resource loader reaches the mapped DLL at 0x200d7bb0, a trivial callback, and then its exported initialization path reaches GetComputerNameW. These are emulated observations, not runtime deployment claims.

The later DLLs import file walking/writing/timestamp APIs, service configuration, Windows token operations, WinHTTP and network-share APIs. The larger one contains Office customUI/VBA templates including OnRibbonLoad and a VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect/CreateThread macro. Imports and templates alone do not establish their final write targets or completed infection paths.
samples.judgment_basis: Patched startup control flow, payload reconstruction and activation, and a self-decoding executable resource graft are unrelated to legitimate installer functionality. No deployment authorization explains these changes.
samples.coverage_gap: The root has two hostile and two suspicious traits. A third independent hostile root behavior is not established by a matchable path. Additional propagation/service/token effects remain in custom-decoded, LZNT1-compressed, header-masked, import-encrypted DLLs. Recovery, API-hash resolution, import decoding and initialization tracing were attempted; file/Office write paths remain unresolved, and the normal extractor does not emulate these loaders. Masked-header concealment now matches both manually recovered stages, but their findings do not roll into the original scan. No duplicate hostile rule was added to reach a quota.
samples.remaining_classifier_disagreement: None for the original after correction: unflagged to hostile (level 25, probability .99). The pre-change classifier missed the malicious file.

samples.marker_line: Apna date picker 0.1.3: upstream React UI; dependencies reviewed
evidence: The original SHA-256 equals the versioned tarball retrieved from the official npm registry for @alsocoder/apna-date-picker@0.1.3. The collector basename omits the scope.

Recovered all 17 original TypeScript/TSX sources from the source map and checked both ESM and CJS output. Component effects synchronize selected dates and calendar focus; handlers parse/format dates, manage popovers, and call caller-supplied change callbacks. No installation hook or hidden module-scope payload was found.
The package exposes single/range/datetime pickers and CSS. prepublishOnly builds with tsup; it is a publishing trigger, not an install-time script.

Fetched and inspected declared direct runtime dependencies at the lower bound of each published range: Radix dismissable-layer 1.1.11, popover 1.1.14, select 2.2.5, clsx 2.1.1, date-fns 4.1.0 and react-day-picker 10.0.1. Their distributed entry points implement UI/date utilities and ordinary build scripts, with no hostile path found. Retrieved the referenced homepage and upstream branch archive; an initial GitHub PURL treated main as a tag and returned 404, so the actual branch URL was fetched.

All 17 of 17 source-map source contents also match the fetched upstream main-branch files after line-ending normalization. The author homepage is a developer site; its application scripts are not imported or executed by the package.
samples.judgment_basis: Recovered runtime behavior matches a React date picker and independently fetched registry bytes match the original. This is positive behavioral/provenance evidence, not an inference from a clean scan.
samples.external_label_explanation: The feed-specific reason is unavailable. The unscoped collector name differs from the real scoped package, making name confusion or feed contamination plausible but unproven.
samples.context_missing: No application deployment context, consuming application code, resolved lockfile or historical dependency-resolution state was supplied. Dependency-range lower bounds were reviewed; the review does not assert every future version in those ranges is safe.
samples.remaining_classifier_disagreement: None: unflagged before and after; all member findings unchanged.

samples.marker_line: Stagehand 4.2 alpha: upstream browser automation; retain capabilities
evidence: The original SHA-256 equals the versioned official npm tarball. All 26 embedded SDK source files in index.mjs.map match the referenced upstream Git commit. The extension ZIP is byte-identical, member by member, to the unpacked extension tree.

The service worker initializes ChromeRuntimeClient/RPCClient/RPCRouter. Requests arrive through the service-worker global __stagehandReceiveFromHost installed by the SDK over an attached CDP session, and responses use the Runtime.addBinding bridge. The manifest has no externally_connectable registration and no arbitrary web-page message-to-OS-command path was established.

Validated RPC methods implement browser navigation, form actions, screenshots, cookie read/write/clear, clipboard operations, page evaluation and response handling. These are documented browser-automation functions with broad debugger/scripting/tabs/all-URL authority, accurately retained as notable capabilities.

Local browser launch finds a Chrome executable, creates a chosen or temporary profile, spawns Chrome with argv and a selected debug port, and polls 127.0.0.1. Cleanup terminates the child or uses taskkill on Windows and deletes temporary profiles. No shell command interpolation or unrelated credential-file collection was established.

Remote sessions use api.browserbase.com or a caller-configured base URL and supplied credentials. LLM requests go to configured model providers; tracing is configured through initialization. Local content-script fetch reads the extension resource. The isolated content script installs locator helpers rather than forwarding arbitrary page postMessage traffic to a shell.

Fetched and inspected direct dependencies @browserbasehq/sdk 2.16.0, @opentelemetry/api 1.9.1, @opentelemetry/core 2.9.0 and zod 4.4.3. Their entry points provide authenticated Browserbase API access, tracing interfaces/core and schema validation. No malicious lifecycle hook or hidden loader was found.
samples.judgment_basis: The published SDK provenance, matching upstream implementation and traced caller-driven browser automation explain the powerful capabilities. No attacker-specific endpoint, unsolicited installation payload or separate hostile path was found.
samples.external_label_explanation: Broad all-site debugger access, cookie/screenshot access, page evaluation and browser process control can resemble browser malware. That is a plausible heuristic explanation; the source did not supply its precise reason.
samples.context_missing: Who invoked the SDK, authorization to operate a particular browser profile, supplied CDP endpoints/model keys and downstream agent instructions are not known. The artifact is likely benign; those deployment choices can still enable abuse.
samples.remaining_classifier_disagreement: None at the calibrated decision level (-1) before/after. The aggregate raw probability .7493571 remains elevated without an alert; it is not treated as a verdict. All archive-member findings remain unchanged.

relocation.reason: The matcher proves a Windows memory-status import, not package concealment or a supply-chain attack. Matcher, description, confidence, notable severity and PE/Windows scope are unchanged. The native-addon debugger/hardware-gate consumer now references the canonical new ID. The preexisting broader symbol observation remains intact.
relocation.audit: Inspected exact and ancestor consumers; broad hidden-payload consumers concerned JavaScript/package manifests and cannot gain or lose this PE import. Equality check of old/new predicates and effective defaults passed.

new_root_claims: mixed-width decoder scattered through host code (suspicious)
rule_review.additional_stage_claim: PNG magic, erased NT signature, shifted pointer and coherent PE32/section headers establish masked-header concealment (suspicious), not successful execution. Both recovered stages match; ordinary PNG, wrong-COFF and reconstructed normal PE controls reject.
rule_review.engine_limit_found: Hex section constraints select only the first identically named section. The resource decoder uses a YARA PE-section iteration to bind the match to any .rsrc, including the second. No broad whole-file bypass was used.
rule_review.material_detection_losses: None. Only the neutral import ID moved, retaining its detection and consumer. No severity was reduced. Every other old original-sample finding retained its ID and severity; both benign packages and all members are identical before/after.

regression.controls: Seven original/mutated PE controls plus four inert shifted-header controls; actual recovered masked DLLs, wrong COFF, ordinary PNG and reconstructed PE also checked. No controls were executed as native programs.
regression.outside_batch_result: Forager-recovered original Expiro control and its two embedded PE units retain every prior finding. Existing testdata/benign/node-addon-import-controls.node also unchanged.
regression.provenance: Fetched packages, upstream repository snapshots, API definition sources and original positive control retain their .forage.json files in the evidence directory.
regression.scan_options: atomscan --no-update --analyze local --mode slow --follow=none -f json; cleave facts for all originals and recovered stages.
regression.scanner_warning: The installed v18 classifier feature spec is older than engine v21 features, both before and after. No thresholds or model files were changed.
